editorial.tldr: DeepSeek's retrained V4-Flash overtook flagship V4 Pro on nine agent benchmarks in late July, then went fully open-source matching Claude Opus-4.8, while price-hike reports built for a week before a "V4 Pro 0813" build quietly appeared on OpenRouter. DeepSeek then confirmed the release as official — now corroborated by four outlets — exiting preview with the anticipated price increase and an unproven "agent gains" claim.
editorial.whats_new: DeepSeek also open-sourced Harness, a free agentic coding tool positioned as a rival to Claude Code, shipping the same day as the pricier V4-Pro API release.
editorial.why_it_matters: The price hike changes the cost math that made V4 Pro competitive against V4-Flash and other cheap agent models, and a free open-source Harness now lets you test DeepSeek's agent stack directly against Claude Code instead of waiting on the vague "agent gains" claim.
editorial.take_for_builders: Re-run your agent benchmark against the price-hiked V4 Pro 0813 build before trusting July's Flash-beats-Pro result, pull the new per-token pricing, and try DeepSeek's open-source Harness against your Claude Code workflows since it's free to test today.

status.detail: DeepSeek's confirmed V4 Pro release exited preview citing agent-capability gains, alongside a Nikkei Asia report of sharply higher user pricing that Chinese press and an analyst note had already flagged a week earlier. DeepSeek also shipped an open-source Harness coding agent the same day; state media has since repeated the launch framing without new figures.

beats.headline: Retrained V4-Flash beats flagship V4 Pro on nine agent benchmarks
beats.summary: DeepSeek's cheaper Flash variant overtakes the company's own Pro model on agent-focused evaluations, then ships as a full open-source release matching Claude Opus-4.8 — a lead a later hands-on finds only partly holds once Pro ships.

beats.headline: Price-hike reports build for a week before DeepSeek confirms anything
beats.summary: China Daily, a CITIC Securities note, and regional coverage all flag a coming DeepSeek price increase days before the official V4 Pro launch makes it real.

beats.headline: A new "V4 Pro 0813" build appears on OpenRouter with no announcement
beats.summary: Simon Willison spots the refreshed Pro model listed API-only, with no DeepSeek announcement page to explain what changed.

beats.headline: Early hands-on says the refreshed Pro's multimodal capabilities meet expectations
beats.summary: The first outside impression of the new build focuses on multimodal quality rather than the agent-benchmark gap Flash had opened.

beats.headline: DeepSeek officially confirms the V4 Pro release
beats.summary: Four outlets — Lufkin Daily News, Reuters, The Information, and Global Times — independently report the Aug 12 OpenRouter build as a deliberate, confirmed release rather than a quiet leak; The Information frames it as a direct challenge to Kimi K3.

beats.headline: Official launch comes with sharply higher user prices
beats.summary: Nikkei Asia reports the confirmed release raises per-user pricing, without breaking out the new rate versus V4-Flash — the increase Chinese press and an analyst note had already flagged a week earlier.

beats.headline: DeepSeek open-sources Harness, a free agentic coding tool pitched against Claude Code
beats.summary: VentureBeat reports the release ships the same day as the pricier V4-Pro API, giving platform engineers a second reason to evaluate the drop.

beats.headline: V4 Pro exits preview status, DeepSeek cites agent-capability gains
beats.summary: The preview-exit framing points at agent gains but no benchmark numbers accompany the claim yet; state broadcaster CGTN and trade outlet Analytics India Magazine both repeat the same "agent capabilities" line over the next day, still without figures.

open_questions: Does V4 Pro's claimed "agent gains" reclaim the benchmark lead V4-Flash took in July, or does Flash remain the stronger agent option?
What benchmark or evaluation backs the "agent gains" claim behind V4 Pro's preview exit?
How large is the new price increase, and does it still make Pro cheaper than V4-Flash per token for agent workloads?
Does DeepSeek publish a technical changelog for V4 Pro 0813 beyond the multimodal- and agent-capability claims?
Does DeepSeek publish benchmarks for the open-sourced Harness tool, and how does it compare to Claude Code on real agentic coding tasks?
